class.name: RoadRelief3D
class.brief_description: A used asphalt street's relief as real geometry that holds puddles.
class.description: Builds a street surface whose ruts, sags and hollows are geometry, so raster, the path tracer and water all see the same bed. The road lies in the node's frame: X along it from 0 to [member length], Z across it from -[member width]/2 to [member width]/2, Y up. Its relief is the sum of a crown (or one cross slope) with gutter pans at the kerbs, two wheel-path ruts per lane with low shoulders (shear rutting's W profile) deepening with [member traffic], ISO 8608 road roughness of [member roughness_class], long settlement sags, birdbath depressions, utility patches and potholes. Every part is a function of world position (cosines with seeded phases, hashed gradient noise, features placed per world cell), so no two streets, or two ends of one, repeat, and pieces laid end to end join without a seam. Moving the node gives a different stretch of street. The mesh is a grid of [member cell] metres with UV and UV2 in metres along and across the road (from the -Z kerb); give it a material with [member GeometryInstance3D.material_override].

method.name: contains
method.description: Whether a world point lies over the road.

method.name: get_height_at
method.description: The height (world Y) of the road surface above or below [param world_position], or -INF where the point is not over the road. Water, props and characters read the same surface the mesh shows.

method.name: local_height
method.description: The relief at a point of the road's frame ([param x] along, [param z] across, metres), as a height in the node's frame. Points past the road are clamped to its edge.

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Rebuilds the mesh and collider now (otherwise they are rebuilt on the next idle frame after any property or transform change).

members.member: The mesh grid's spacing (metres). The ruts and hollows are geometry at this scale; finer texture belongs in the material.
When enabled, a static body with the same surface (a trimesh) is built under the node.
The collision layers of the static body.
The fall from the crown to each kerb, as rise over run (AASHTO: 1.5 to 2 % on paved streets).
Birdbath depressions (local settlement where water stands after rain) per 100 m², placed by a hash of world cells.
The deepest birdbath depression (metres).
How far the gutter pan falls below the cross slope at the kerb (metres).
The gutter pan's width along each kerb (metres).
Lanes across the road; each has two wheel-path ruts.
The road's length along its X axis (metres).
When enabled, the road falls one way, toward +Z, instead of from a crown to both kerbs.
Utility patches per 100 m²: rectangles cut square to the street, a few millimetres proud or sunk with a stepped edge.
Potholes per 100 m²: ragged, steep-walled hollows.
The deepest pothole (metres).
The ISO 8608 roughness class of the surface: its displacement spectrum Gd(n) = Gd(n0) (n / n0)^-2 over wavelengths 0.12 to 3 m.
Rut depth (metres) at full [member traffic].
The long settlement sags' amplitude (metres), over 9 and 24 m.
Varies every part of the relief; the relief also follows world position, so the same seed differs from place to place.
The distance between a lane's two wheel paths (metres).
How worn the wheel paths are: 0 a quiet lane, 1 a bus route. The ruts deepen and fade along the street around this.
The road's width kerb to kerb (metres).

constants.constant: ISO 8608 class A, very good: Gd(n0) = 16e-6 m³.
